notes.summary: A synonym is a word with the same or nearly the same meaning. SSC gives a word (alone or in a sentence) and asks for its synonym. Regular reading plus daily flashcards is the only reliable preparation; roots and elimination help on the day.

concepts.title: Same meaning, same part of speech
concepts.body: The answer must match the given word's part of speech. If the word is an adjective (candid), the synonym is an adjective (frank), not a noun (frankness).

concepts.title: Use roots and prefixes
concepts.body:
• bene- = good (benevolent = kind)
  • mal- = bad (malicious = spiteful)
  • loqu- = speak (loquacious = talkative)
  • -cide = kill; omni- = all; chron- = time

concepts.title: Context sentences
concepts.body: When the word is in a sentence, the meaning in that sentence counts. The novel idea impressed everyone → novel = new, not 'book'.

varieties.name: Direct word
varieties.how: Recall the meaning; if unsure, use roots and eliminate options with the opposite sense.

varieties.name: Word in a sentence
varieties.how: Read the sentence, decide the meaning used there, then match.

example.q: The old man's frugal habits helped him save a fortune.
steps: Saving a fortune suggests careful spending.

tips: Eliminate any option that is an antonym; SSC often places the antonym as a trap.
Learn words in pairs (word + synonym) from flashcards daily.
Check part of speech before choosing.
traps: Words that look or sound similar: eminent (famous) vs imminent (about to happen).
A word with a related but different meaning: stingy is not a synonym of frugal in a positive context.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Candid
questions.solution: Candid means honest and straightforward = Frank. Secretive is close to its opposite.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Abundant
questions.solution: Abundant = existing in large quantities = Plentiful. Scarce is the antonym.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bold word.
Her meticulous notes made it easy for the team to repeat the experiment.
questions.solution: Notes that let others repeat an experiment must be very detailed and careful. Meticulous = Painstaking.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Loquacious

Select the most appropriate synonym of the bold word.
The committee's decision was arbitrary; no one could explain the reasons behind it.
questions.solution: A decision without explainable reasons is based on whim. Arbitrary = Capricious. Judicious (wise, well judged) is nearly the opposite.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Ephemeral
questions.solution: Ephemeral = lasting a very short time = Transient. Ethereal (delicate, heavenly) is a look-alike trap; Eternal is the antonym.
